title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, benefit Events
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, benefit Events] We want to host a fundraiser but don't have a budget for a venue. What do we do?

Find a comrade with a backyard or a local dive bar that hates the status quo as much as we do. Throw a rent party with local bands or a radical trivia night where the entry fee goes straight into the war chest. You don't need a ballroom when you have a community willing to pack into a basement for the cause. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: District Attorney races
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[District Attorney races] A friend asked me: 'How does a radical DA change anything without changing the law?' What do I tell them?

The law is a weapon, and the DA chooses where to point it. You stop prosecuting low-level drug offenses, refuse to seek the death penalty, and go after wage theft and corporate polluters instead of the poor. It’s about taking the boot off the necks of our people by exercising the power of non-prosecution. Turn that office into a consumer protection agency for the working class and a nightmare for the exploitative bosses.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, two-Factor Authentication
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, two-Factor Authentication] Is using my phone number for 2FA safe?

It’s a trap. SIM swapping is a common tactic where someone convinces your carrier to move your number to their phone, giving them access to all your accounts. Use an authentication app like Aegis or a physical security key like a YubiKey instead. Never use your phone number as a security layer if you can avoid it; it's the weakest link in the chain.

title: Karl Organizing: Jail Support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Jail Support] What do we do when our comrades get arrested at a protest?

Real talk: Karl's answer: Get to the precinct immediately and wait there until the last person is released so they know they aren't alone. Have a lawyer on call and a bail fund ready to go before the march even starts. Bring water, snacks, and phone chargers for the folks walking out of those cells.

title: Karl Organizing: Accountability
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Accountability] Can you explain: what if one group isn't doing the work they promised to do?

Have a direct, face-to-face conversation and ask them what the bottleneck is. If they are overwhelmed, offer help; if they are just being lazy or posturing, tell them they are holding back the whole movement. We don't have time for passengers when we're trying to sink the billionaire's ship, so everyone has to pull their weight or get out of the way. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Rejecting Corporate Cash
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Rejecting Corporate Cash] Can you explain: a local real estate developer offered to sponsor our community garden. Take it?

Here's the thing: Absolutely not. Those developers are the ones driving your neighbors out of their homes; taking their money is just helping them paint a smiley face on displacement. If they want to help the garden, they can stop hiking the rent. We'll fund our own soil and seeds through bake sales and tool-shares before we take a bribe from a landlord.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: phone Security
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: phone Security] Give me the short version: Can the police force me to unlock my phone during a protest?

Disable your face-ID and thumbprint locks before you even leave the house; use a long passcode they can't just point at your face to bypass. If they demand your phone, tell them you do not consent to a search and stay silent. Your digital life is a map of our movement's networks, so protect it like you're guarding a comrade's life.

title: Karl Organizing: Phone Hygiene
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Phone Hygiene] A friend asked me: 'What's the best way to back up my phone before an action?' What do I tell them?

Back it up to a local hard drive at home, then encrypt that drive with a strong password. Turn off all auto-syncing to the cloud—Apple and Google will hand over your 'private' backups the moment the state asks. Once your backup is safe at home, wipe any sensitive messages or photos from the device you're carrying. Travel light and travel clean. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, de-escalation
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, de-escalation] How can we handle a neighborhood dispute without calling the cops?

Cops only bring guns to a conversation, so we handle our own business by sending a small team of neutral neighbors to listen to both sides. Focus on the harm done and how to fix it rather than who broke what rule. If things get heated, separate the parties and let tempers cool before trying to find a resolution. We build safety through relationships and accountability, not through handcuffs and cages.

title: Karl Organizing: Unionizing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Unionizing] How do I start a union at my job without getting fired?

Karl's answer: Start secret one-on-one conversations with your most trusted coworkers away from the boss's prying eyes. Map out every department to see who's ready to fight and who might be a snitch. Once you have a solid majority of the shop, contact a local organizer to file your cards and go public with a bang.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: intervention Ethics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: intervention Ethics] Give me the short version: When should I actually step in if I see a cop harassing someone?

Assess the situation and ask the person being harassed if they want help before you dive in. If they say yes, start filming and ask the officer for their name and badge number while standing at a safe distance. Sometimes just having three or four people watching silently with phones out is enough to make a bully in uniform back off. Solidarity means following the lead of the person in the crosshairs.

title: Karl Organizing: Childcare Collectives
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Childcare Collectives] Can you explain: how can we support the parents in our organizing circle who can't find sitters?

Build a childcare rotation where those of us without kids take shifts watching the little ones during meetings and actions. It's not 'babysitting'; it's revolutionary support that allows parents—especially moms—to lead the fight. Make sure there's a safe, fun space with snacks and activities so the kids actually want to be there. We raise the next generation of rebels together, as a village, not as isolated nuclear families.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: two-Factor Authentication
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: two-Factor Authentication] Give me the short version: Is using my phone number for 2FA safe?

Here's the thing: It’s a trap. SIM swapping is a common tactic where someone convinces your carrier to move your number to their phone, giving them access to all your accounts. Use an authentication app like Aegis or a physical security key like a YubiKey instead. Never use your phone number as a security layer if you can avoid it; it's the weakest link in the chain.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: eviction Defense
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: eviction Defense] Give me the short version: A neighbor is getting evicted tomorrow morning. How do we stop it?

Pack the hallway with thirty comrades and make it physically impossible for the sheriff to reach the door. Bring coffee, bring music, and bring a loud megaphone to let the landlord know the whole neighborhood is watching their cruelty. While you're holding the line, have your legal team file every emergency motion possible to gum up the works. We don't let our people get thrown to the curb while billionaires' apartments sit empty and rotting.

title: Karl Organizing: Secure Document Sharing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Secure Document Sharing] How can I send sensitive files to my organizing committee safely?

Real talk: Stop using Google Drive or Dropbox; those companies are just extensions of the state surveillance machine. Use OnionShare or a password-protected, encrypted zip file sent through an end-to-end encrypted channel. If the document is truly dangerous, put it on a thumb drive and hand it over in person. Digital trails are permanent; physical hand-offs are much harder to intercept.

title: Karl Organizing: Running for Office
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Running for Office] How can a regular worker like me run for city council?

Real talk: Karl's answer: Don't wait for the party bosses to give you permission—just get the signatures you need from your neighbors. Run on a platform of real shit like rent control and public transit, not vague slogans. Use your campaign as an organizing tool to build power in the streets that lasts long after election day.

title: Karl Organizing: Rotating Roles
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Rotating Roles] A friend asked me: 'Should the same person always be the spokesperson for the coalition?' What do I tell them?

Absolutely not, because that creates a bottleneck and a target for the bosses to bribe or smear. Train as many comrades as possible to speak to the press and lead the meetings so the movement doesn't collapse if one person gets sick or arrested. A leaderless movement is hard to stop, but a leader-full movement where everyone is capable is invincible.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: decision Making
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: decision Making] Give me the short version: How do we make decisions without spending hours arguing over every detail?

Use a '70% agreement' rule for the big stuff and delegate the small stuff to specialized working groups. You don't need a full assembly to decide what color the flyers are; you need a few trusted comrades to just get it done. If you try to reach perfect consensus on everything, the billionaires will have bought another yacht before you've even picked a meeting spot. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Enemy Propaganda
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Enemy Propaganda] Can you explain: the local news is lying about our coalition. How do we fight back?

Stop begging the corporate media for scraps of coverage and become your own media outlet. Use your combined social media reach, print your own newsletters, and talk directly to your neighbors on their doorsteps. When the billionaires own the newspapers, the only truth people will hear is the truth you tell them face-to-face and the results they see with their own eyes. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Escalation Management
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Escalation Management] Can you explain: what if the police get aggressive while we are watching them?

Hold your ground but don't give them an easy excuse to start swinging or shooting. Keep your cameras high and clearly state that you are peacefully observing. If they move in, back up slowly as a group, keeping your eyes on them the whole time. The goal is to survive to share the footage and keep the focus on their misconduct, not to end up in a hospital bed. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Identifying Undercovers
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Identifying Undercovers] A friend asked me: 'How can we tell if someone at our meeting is an infiltrator?' What do I tell them?

Watch for the person who pushes for illegal or violent action way too early or asks too many questions about people's private lives. Real comrades focus on the work and build trust over time through small, consistent actions. Don't get paranoid, but keep sensitive info on a need-to-know basis. If someone smells like a cop, they probably are; trust your gut and move the planning to a smaller circle. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Account Security
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Account Security] What should I do if I think my account was hacked?

Here's the thing: Assume the device is compromised. Use a different, clean device to change your master passwords and revoke all active sessions. Alert your comrades immediately so they don't fall for any phishing links sent from your account. If we don't look out for each other, the enemy wins. Once the breach is contained, wipe the infected device and start fresh.

title: Karl Organizing: Night Safety
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Night Safety] How can we keep the neighborhood safe at night without more patrols?

Organize 'walking school buses' or evening stroll groups so nobody has to walk alone if they don't want to. Fix broken streetlights ourselves or install motion-sensor lights in dim areas with the permission of the residents. Increasing positive foot traffic is the best way to discourage actual harm. We light up the dark with solidarity, not with police sirens.

title: Karl Organizing: Testing the strength
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Testing the strength] How do we know if our supporters are actually ready to vote 'yes'?

You give them a 'structure test.' Ask them to do something small but visible, like wearing a union button or signing a public petition for better breakroom fans. If they won't wear a button, they might not vote 'yes' when the boss is breathing down their neck. These tests show you exactly where your support is strong and where you need to do more 1-on-1 work. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Start a union: first steps
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Start a union: first steps] I want to start a union at my job. Where do I even begin?

Real talk: Start with one-on-ones. Not a group chat, not a flyer — private conversations with the coworkers you trust most. Ask what's pissing them off. You'll hear the same three grievances from everyone, and those become your organizing issues. Map the shop: who leads, who follows, who'd rat. When you've got a solid core, THEN call an organizer.

title: Karl Organizing: Resource Sharing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Resource Sharing] How do we handle money and tools between different groups?

Create a shared pool of resources where the groups with more cash chip in to help the groups with more people. Total transparency is the only way this works, so keep a public ledger that every member can see. Share the bullhorns, the high-speed printers, and the mailing lists like they belong to the movement, because the bosses already own everything else.

title: Karl Organizing: Bail Prep
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Bail Prep] A friend asked me: 'How do I handle bail if I don't have much money?' What do I tell them?

Here's how it works: Before the action, identify a local community bail fund or pool resources with your affinity group to create an emergency pot. We look out for our own, and we don't let billionaires' prices keep our comrades in cages. If you're inside, wait for the word from legal support; we are coming to get you out.

title: Karl Organizing: Secure Document Sharing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Secure Document Sharing] A friend asked me: 'Is email safe if I use a provider like Proton?' What do I tell them?

Here's the thing: It's better than Gmail, but it's not a silver bullet. If you're emailing someone on a regular server, that message is exposed the second it leaves Proton's walls. For real security, keep the sensitive talk inside Signal or use PGP encryption if you're technical. Treat email like a postcard that a cop might read at any sorting facility. Keep it brief and keep it clean.

title: Karl Organizing: Jail support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Jail support] How does jail support work at protests?

One person stays out — never gets arrested — with a list of everyone inside, their legal names, and emergency contacts. They call the legal hotline, track who's where, and meet people at release with food, water, and a ride. Jail support is unglamorous and absolutely essential. Volunteer for it. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: food Sourcing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: food Sourcing] Give me the short version: We have a fridge but it's always empty. Where do we get enough food to keep it full?

Here's how it works: Talk to the managers at local independent grocers and bakeries about their 'waste'—most of them hate throwing good food away but follow corporate rules. Organize a weekly grocery run where neighbors buy one extra staple item to drop off, and coordinate with local farms for their surplus harvests. We don't need charity; we need to redirect the abundance the capitalists are prepared to rot in a dumpster. Pool resources to buy in bulk when things are on sale.

title: Karl Organizing: Permits
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Permits] Do we really need to get a permit before we hit the streets?

Here's the thing: Permits are just the cops telling you where you are allowed to be harmless. If you want a parade, get a permit; if you want to disrupt the flow of capital, you don't ask for permission. Just know that going rogue means you need a tighter crew and a solid legal plan, because the state will not protect anyone who actually threatens a billionaire's bottom line.

title: Karl Organizing: Sustaining the Fight
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Sustaining the Fight] Can you explain: how do we keep people from burning out on rapid response?

Here's the thing: Rotate your shifts and make sure nobody is on call 24/7 or they'll be useless within a month. Celebrate your wins, no matter how small, and make time for communal meals and joy that have nothing to do with the pigs. This is a marathon, not a sprint, and we need every comrade healthy and sharp for the long haul. Rest is a radical act when the state wants you exhausted.

title: Karl Organizing: Scaling Up
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Scaling Up] How do we grow from a local coalition to something bigger?

Look, Find coalitions in the next town over that are fighting the same boss or the same landlord and link your demands. You don't need a massive national headquarters; you need a network of local groups that can strike or protest simultaneously to paralyze the system. Power is built from the bottom up, one block and one shop floor at a time, until the whole structure shakes.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: after the Win
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: after the Win] Give me the short version: What happens to the coalition once we actually win our main demand?

Don't you dare go home and think the job is done. Use the structure you built to find the next target, because the billionaires will be plotting to take back what you just won the second you stop looking. A coalition shouldn't just be for one crisis; it should be the foundation for a permanent power base that the ruling class can never dismantle. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, crowd Logistics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, crowd Logistics] How do we stay organized when things get chaotic in the street?

Use the 'buddy system' so nobody is ever standing alone or getting snatched without a witness. Assign roles like 'scout,' 'vibe checker,' and 'legal' so everyone knows exactly what their job is when the pressure starts. If the group needs to move, do it together in a tight block rather than scattering. A disorganized crowd is a target; an organized community is a force. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: sustaining the Work
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: sustaining the Work] Give me the short version: I'm exhausted and feel like I'm burning out. How do I keep going?

Here's how it works: Take a damn break and let the rest of the collective carry the load for a while. Mutual aid isn't a solo performance; it's a relay race where we pass the baton when our legs get heavy. If you burn yourself out, you're no good to the movement or your neighbors, so go rest and recharge. We're in this for the long haul, and that means pacing ourselves so we can see the revolution through to the end.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: the First Meeting
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: the First Meeting] Give me the short version: What is the most important thing to do at our very first coalition meeting?

Real talk: Set a specific goal and a hard deadline for the first action before anyone leaves the room. Don't spend two hours introducing yourselves and sharing 'vibes'; identify the common enemy and decide on a date to make them sweat. A coalition that doesn't act immediately is just a book club with better slogans, and we are here to win, not study.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, clinic Defense
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, clinic Defense] What do I do if I see harassers blocking a healthcare clinic?

Look, Show up with a group of comrades and use your bodies to create a physical corridor for patients to walk through safely. Wear bright vests so you're easily identified as the good guys and keep your backs to the harassers to avoid being baited into a shouting match. Your job isn't to debate bigots; it's to be a human shield for someone just trying to access care. Stay calm, stay focused, and keep the path clear.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, debate Strategy
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, debate Strategy] How do I handle a debate with a 'moderate' incumbent?

Here's the thing: Don't let them hide behind 'incremental change' or 'budgetary constraints.' Call out their failures directly: show the people the tent cities that grew on their watch and the luxury condos they approved while residents were priced out. Pivot every technical question back to the material reality of the voters. Be the only person on that stage who speaks like a human being rather than a walking press release.

title: Karl Organizing: Burner Devices
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Burner Devices] How do I get a burner phone without looking suspicious?

Don't go to the shop next to your house, and for the love of the movement, pay with cash. Buy a cheap flip phone and a prepaid SIM at a big box store where you're just another face in the crowd. Never turn it on at your house or link it to your personal accounts. A burner is for the mission, not for checking your personal emails.

title: Karl Organizing: Coalition Building
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Coalition Building] How do I bring different groups together for one campaign?

Find the common enemy: the developers, the corporate lobbyists, and the politicians who serve them. Show the environmentalists that their fight is the same as the housing advocates' fight, because the same people are destroying the air and the neighborhood. Build the campaign around a 'People’s Charter' that reflects the shared needs of the entire working class. Unity isn't about everyone agreeing on everything; it's about everyone fighting the same fight together.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: sustainer Programs
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: sustainer Programs] Give me the short version: Is it better to ask for one big check or small monthly amounts?

Give me ten comrades chipping in ten bucks a month over one guy writing a thousand-dollar check any day of the week. Monthly sustainers provide the predictable floor we need to plan long-term campaigns without panicking about the rent. It builds a base of people who are spiritually and financially committed to the long haul, not just a one-time thrill.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: local Press
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: local Press] Give me the short version: The local paper is biased against me. How do I get my message out?

Stop begging them for coverage and start making your own media. Record your own videos, write your own newsletters, and use your volunteers to spread the word through every apartment building in the district. When the press does show up, be polite but firm, and always bring the conversation back to your platform. If they won't tell the truth about the struggle, we'll shout it from every porch until they can't ignore us.

title: Karl Organizing: Small Group Value
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Small Group Value] Is it worth the time joining up with tiny local groups that only have five members?

Here's how it works: A hundred pebbles make a landslide if you throw them at the same time. Those tiny groups have deep roots in their specific neighborhoods that your big city organization will never have. Respect their local knowledge, share your printing press and bullhorns, and build a front that the bosses can't ignore just by looking at a map.

title: Karl Organizing: Eviction Defense
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Eviction Defense] A friend asked me: 'A neighbor is getting evicted tomorrow morning. How do we stop it?' What do I tell them?

Pack the hallway with thirty comrades and make it physically impossible for the sheriff to reach the door. title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, in-kind Donations
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, in-kind Donations] Someone wants to give us gear instead of cash. Is that helpful?

Hell yes, take the gear and put it to work immediately. If a comrade has a high-end printer, a PA system, or a van they aren't using, that's thousands of dollars we don't have to raise ourselves. Every physical asset we own is a tool for the struggle, so catalog it, maintain it, and make sure it's always ready for the next mobilization.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: ethical Banking
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: ethical Banking] Give me the short version: Where should we keep the movement's cash so it's safe?

Here's how it works: Get your money out of the big Wall Street banks that fund pipelines and private prisons yesterday. Move the war chest to a local credit union or a community-owned bank where the staff actually knows your name. It won't solve capitalism, but at least your deposits aren't being used as a weapon against your own comrades while you sleep.

title: Karl Organizing: Inoculation
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Inoculation] My boss is starting to act really nice all of a sudden. What gives?

That's the 'Love Bomb,' and it's a total scam. They'll buy pizza, hold 'town halls,' and pretend to care about your feelings because they're terrified of your power. You need to warn your coworkers right now: the boss is only being nice to trick you into staying weak. Tell everyone to enjoy the free pizza while they plan their next move to take the whole bakery. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Rejecting Corporate Cash
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Rejecting Corporate Cash] A local real estate developer offered to sponsor our community garden. Take it?

Here's how it works: Absolutely not. Those developers are the ones driving your neighbors out of their homes; taking their money is just helping them paint a smiley face on displacement. If they want to help the garden, they can stop hiking the rent. We'll fund our own soil and seeds through bake sales and tool-shares before we take a bribe from a landlord.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, donor Capture
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, donor Capture] A wealthy businessman wants to give us a large sum but has some 'suggestions' on our messaging. Should we take it?

Here's the thing: Tell him to keep his blood money and his opinions. The second you let a fat cat dictate your slogans is the second you stop being a threat to his class. If he wants to help, he can drop the cash in the bucket and walk away with no strings attached; otherwise, he's just buying a leash to put on your movement.

title: Karl Organizing: Body Cameras
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Body Cameras] Will the officers' body cameras prove they were being violent?

Don't count on it; those cameras 'malfunction' the second a pig decides to use his baton. This is why we need our own cameras on every corner and in every hand. Their footage belongs to the state, but our footage belongs to the people, and that's the only truth that matters. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Clothing Swaps
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Clothing Swaps] Can you explain: we have a ton of donated clothes. How do we distribute them effectively?

Real talk: Forget the 'sorting center' model; just set up some racks in a public park and let people take what they need for free. Organize them by size and type so it doesn't look like a pile of trash, and make sure the winter gear is front and center when the temperature drops. If you have leftovers, get them to the local shelters or encampments directly. Dignity means being able to pick out your own coat without someone watching over your shoulder.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: social Media OPSEC
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: social Media OPSEC] Give me the short version: Is it okay to tag my friends in photos from the community garden?

Never tag anyone in any political context without their explicit, enthusiastic consent. Tagging creates a digital map of our networks for the state to study. Even a 'wholesome' garden project can be used to build a profile on organizers. Let people manage their own digital footprint; don't do the feds' job for them by building their database.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: anti-Harassment Tactics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: anti-Harassment Tactics] Give me the short version: How do we deal with aggressive 'sidewalk counselors' at clinics?

Use umbrellas and banners to block their signs and keep them from filming patients' faces. Play loud, upbeat music to drown out their harassment so patients don't have to hear their vitriol. Don't try to win an argument with someone who thinks they're on a mission from god; just neutralize their tools. We are the wall between the vulnerable and the hateful.

title: Karl Organizing: Social Media OPSEC
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Social Media OPSEC] I want to post photos of the march to inspire people, is that okay?

Inspiration is good, but snitching is better for the enemy. Before you post, use an app to scrub the metadata—that's the hidden digital tag that tells the feds exactly where and when the photo was taken. Blur every single face, including the background. If you don't have time to redact the identities of your comrades, keep that photo on your drive and out of the cloud.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, crowdfunding Platforms
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, crowdfunding Platforms] Which website should we use to raise money online?

Avoid the big corporate platforms that take a massive cut and can freeze your funds the moment a right-wing rag complains. Look for worker-owned cooperatives or movement-aligned tech that prioritizes security and low fees. Better yet, set up a direct portal on your own site so the vultures don't get a single penny of the community's support. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Rapid Response
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Rapid Response] A friend asked me: 'How do we mobilize the whole coalition quickly when something bad happens?' What do I tell them?

Set up a phone tree or an encrypted signal blast that can reach every member in under ten minutes. You need a 'break glass in case of emergency' plan where everyone knows exactly which street corner to stand on when the cops show up or the layoffs start. Speed is our only advantage against the slow, bloated bureaucracy of the state and the corporations. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: phone Hygiene
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: phone Hygiene] Give me the short version: What's the best way to back up my phone before an action?

Back it up to a local hard drive at home, then encrypt that drive with a strong password. Turn off all auto-syncing to the cloud—Apple and Google will hand over your 'private' backups the moment the state asks. Once your backup is safe at home, wipe any sensitive messages or photos from the device you're carrying. Travel light and travel clean. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: School Board tactics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[School Board tactics] Can you explain: what can a leftist actually do on a school board?

You stop the privatization ghouls from gutting the classrooms to fund their charter school scams. Fight for universal free meals and kick the cops out of the hallways so kids can actually learn without being treated like prisoners. Use that seat to protect teachers' unions and ensure history is taught as a struggle for the people, not a fairytale for the billionaires. It’s the front line against the right-wing attempt to colonize our children's futures.
